plan: Compute QK-transpose scores, optionally scale by the key dimension, normalize each query row with softmax, then use those weights to mix V.
title: How scaled dot-product attention mixes values
audience: A second-year engineering undergraduate who knows vectors, matrices, and basic probability but has not studied Transformers.

starting_point.idea: Each query compares with every key; the resulting weights decide how much of each value vector contributes to that query's output.
starting_point.why: Following the scores, row-wise probabilities, and weighted values makes the attention calculation inspectable one operation at a time.
starting_point.explanation: For matrices Q, K, and V, compute S = QK^T / sqrt(d_k) when scaling is enabled, apply softmax separately to each row of S, and multiply those weights by V. Rows of the weight matrix sum to one.

symbols.meaning: Rows are key vectors compared with each query
Rows are value vectors mixed by the attention weights

Query-key dot-product score matrix, optionally scaled

controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Each row is one query. The two columns are its two features.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Each row is a key compared with each query.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Each row is a value vector that attention can mix.

controls.label: Scale scores by 1/sqrt(d_k)
controls.help: Turn scaling off to compare the same dot products before and after dividing by sqrt(2).

visuals.title: Scores: query rows by key columns

explorations.title: Make all scores equal
explorations.instruction: Apply the preset. Compare the score and weight matrices, then inspect the mixed values.
explorations.observe: Every score is zero, so each query assigns one half of its weight to each key and receives the average of the two value rows.
explorations.why: Softmax maps equal scores to equal probabilities; the output is therefore the uniform weighted average.

explorations.title: Make one key dominate
explorations.instruction: Apply the preset. Compare the two score columns and see how strongly each query favors the first value.
explorations.observe: Each query scores the first key 4/sqrt(2) and the second key zero, so most of its output comes from the first value row.
explorations.why: A larger score receives a larger share after softmax; scaling reduces the score gap before normalization.

limitation: This fixed two-query, two-key example omits masking, batching, positional information, learned projections, multiple heads, and training. The matrices are directly editable teaching inputs, not parameters learned from data.

grounding.locator: Vaswani et al. (2017), Section 3.2.1, Scaled Dot-Product Attention; arXiv HTML version 1706.03762v7
grounding.claim: The section defines attention as a softmax of query-key dot products scaled by the square root of the key dimension, multiplied by V.

tests.name: identity matrices with scaling produce the stated attention and weighted values
disabling scaling changes softmax concentration but keeps the weighted value calculation
equal scores yield uniform weights and average the values
dominant first key controls the weighted value

invariants.name: each query distributes one unit of attention across keys

compute_js: function compute(inputs) { const Q = inputs.queries; const K = inputs.keys; const V = inputs.values; const factor = inputs.scale ? 1 / Math.sqrt(2) : 1; const scores = [[(Q[0][0] * K[0][0] + Q[0][1] * K[0][1]) * factor, (Q[0][0] * K[1][0] + Q[0][1] * K[1][1]) * factor], [(Q[1][0] * K[0][0] + Q[1][1] * K[0][1]) * factor, (Q[1][0] * K[1][0] + Q[1][1] * K[1][1]) * factor]]; function softmax2(row) { const high = Math.max(row[0], row[1]); const a = Math.exp(row[0] - high); const b = Math.exp(row[1] - high); const total = a + b; return [a / total, b / total]; } const weights = [softmax2(scores[0]), softmax2(scores[1])]; const output = weights.map(row => [row[0] * V[0][0] + row[1] * V[1][0], row[0] * V[0][1] + row[1] * V[1][1]]); return { score_matrix: scores, attention_weights: weights, attended_values: output }; }
